messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: 
The current bug report states that when extracting string values from XML elements using JXPath, leading and trailing spaces are being trimmed unexpectedly. The test `testPreserveDOM()` calls `doTest("preserve", DocumentContainer.MODEL_DOM, " foo ")` which means it expects the string value to preserve spaces around "foo".

Inspecting the test reveals that `doTest` creates a JXPathContext and asserts the value retrieved for a given XPath expression equals the expected value, including leading/trailing spaces.

Looking into how the value string is obtained from the XML node in the DOM model, the method `DOMNodePointer.getValue()` returns `stringValue(node)`. The `stringValue(Node)` method is responsible for retrieving the string content of an XML node.

Upon examining `stringValue(Node)`, we see:

- For comment, text, and processing instruction nodes, it returns their data or value trimmed with `text.trim()`. This means leading and trailing spaces are explicitly removed at this level.
- For element nodes (or others), it iterates child nodes, recursively collects text nodes' values (without trimming each addition), but ultimately does `buf.toString().trim()` before returning. This final trim again removes leading and trailing spaces.

This double trim effectively removes the leading and trailing whitespace that might exist in the XML text content, which matches the bug report description of trimming spaces.

Hence, the cause of the bug is in `stringValue(Node)` in `DOMNodePointer` class, where the code uses `String.trim()` at multiple points, including for text nodes and finally on the concatenated string, which causes any leading/trailing spaces to be lost when extracting string values from XML nodes.

This behavior causes the test expecting " foo " to fail since the returned string is trimmed.

No relevant recent bug reports were found to contradict or deepen the analysis, so this diagnosis is based solely on the test, bug report, and code inspection.

The fix would involve removing or modifying the trim calls in `DOMNodePointer.stringValue(Node)` to preserve leading and trailing spaces as expected by the user.

Hence the bug lies in `DOMNodePointer.stringValue(Node)` implementation.

---

Next, I will suggest which methods should be fixed.
org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.model.dom.DOMNodePointer.stringValue(org.w3c.dom.Node)

Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
